trial_court: Family Court, Bilaspur in Civil Suit No. 331-A/2019
case_name: Ku. Durgesh Nandani vs Neelam Sharma

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Ku. Durgesh Nandani, D/o Brajmohan Duwa, Aged About 44 Years, R/o Link Road Infront of Bukhari Petrol Pump Bilaspur Chhattisgarh.
parties.respondent_defendant: Neelam Sharma, Daughter of Late Brijmohan Dua and Wife of Shri Rajendra Sharma, Aged About 42 Years, Resident of Gondpara, Beside Agrawal Saw Mill, Bilaspur, District - Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh.

facts_of_case: The appellants sought a declaration of paternity against the defendant Brajmohan Duwa, which was dismissed by the trial court. The present appeal has been preferred against this judgment.

legal_principles.principle: The fact that any person was born during the continuance of a valid marriage between his mother and any man, or within two hundred and eighty days after its dissolution, the mother remaining unmarried, shall be conclusive proof that he is the legitimate son of that man, unless it can be shown that the parties to the marriage had no access to each other at any time when he could have been begotten.
legal_principles.held: This section provides that conclusive proof of legitimacy is equivalent to paternity

legal_principles.principle: There exists a strong presumption that the husband is the father of the child borne by his wife during the subsistence of their marriage.
legal_principles.held: This section makes it abundantly clear that there exists a strong presumption that the husband is the father of the child borne by his wife during the subsistence of their marriage.
